| Notes | Writes data | `create_many_notes` |

## Description

The description the MCP server sends to the model, word for word. Its rules apply to every call.

> Create multiple notes at once. Each note's content body must be in Markdown format. Each note can have its own status, tags, auto-restack delay (autoRestackAfterHours), link-preview choice (includePreviews), optional imageUrl (remote image URLs, max 5 per note — fetched and stored like CSV import), Buffer channels (bufferChannelIds), and per-channel Buffer posts (bufferChannelPosts). If any content includes a link, ask the user if they'd like link previews before calling this tool; pass includePreviews: true only for notes where they confirm. You SHOULD ask the user which tags to apply before calling this — use list_tags first to show available tags if needed. Tags also control which reserved queue times the notes can take when later scheduled (OR match; untagged notes only use open or untagged-only times). When generating new note content, call get_writing_style first unless the user already pasted complete style instructions. Call list_buffer_channels first if setting Buffer channels or per-channel posts.

## Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `notes` | `object[]` | Yes | Array of notes to create (1–50) Min items 1. Max items 50. |
| `notes[].autoRestackAfterHours` | `integer \| null` | No | Optional auto-restack delay in hours (1–168). If set, after the note is published WriteStack will automatically restack (re-post) it the given number of hours later to boost visibility. Leave this field out unless the user asks for a specific auto-restack choice: when creating a note, leaving it out applies the user's default auto-restack setting, and when scheduling or updating, leaving it out keeps the note's current value. Pass null ONLY when the user explicitly asks to turn auto-restack off. Requires the WriteStack browser extension v1.4.78 or higher to actually fire. Min 1. Max 168. |
| `notes[].bufferChannelIds` | `string[]` | No | Optional array of Buffer channel IDs to cross-post this new note to once it publishes on Substack. Call list_buffer_channels first to get the valid IDs — only IDs returned by that tool are accepted. Maximum 20 channels per note — requests with more are rejected. Channel IDs from bufferChannelPosts are merged in automatically. Omit or pass an empty array to skip Buffer cross-posting unless you also pass bufferChannelPosts. Requires a connected Buffer account. Platform limits still apply: Instagram requires an image or video, and Instagram feed images must be between 4:5 and 1.91:1 aspect ratio for automatic posting (otherwise Buffer falls back to Notify Me). See https://support.buffer.com/article/622-instagrams-accepted-aspect-ratio-ranges |
| `notes[].bufferChannelPosts` | `object[]` | No | Optional per-channel Buffer post overrides when a channel should have different text or images than the Substack note. Call list_buffer_channels first. Each item needs bufferChannelId and, unless reset is true, a plain-text body (max 5000). Those channel IDs are also selected on the note (merged with bufferChannelIds, still max 20). imageUrl attaches images to that channel only — they are not added to the Substack note. Omit imageUrl to keep existing channel images; pass [] to clear them. includePreviews adds a link card from the first URL in that channel's body (max 1). reset: true deletes the override so the channel falls back to the note. Removing a channel from bufferChannelIds does not delete a saved override. Platform limits still apply: Instagram requires an image or video, and Instagram feed images must be between 4:5 and 1.91:1 aspect ratio for automatic posting (otherwise Buffer falls back to Notify Me). See https://support.buffer.com/article/622-instagrams-accepted-aspect-ratio-ranges Max items 20. |
| `notes[].bufferChannelPosts[].body` | `string` | No | Plain-text override for this channel (max 5000). Required unless reset is true. This is what Buffer publishes for this channel instead of the Substack note. Max length 5000. |
| `notes[].bufferChannelPosts[].bufferChannelId` | `string` | Yes | Buffer channel ID from list_buffer_channels |
| `notes[].bufferChannelPosts[].imageUrl` | `string[]` | No | Remote image URLs for this channel only (max 5). WriteStack fetches and stores them. They are not added to the Substack note. Omit to keep existing channel images; pass [] to clear them. Max items 5. |
| `notes[].bufferChannelPosts[].includePreviews` | `boolean` | No | If true, attach a rich link-preview card from the first URL in this channel's body. Max 1 preview per channel. |
| `notes[].bufferChannelPosts[].reset` | `boolean` | No | If true, delete this channel's custom post so it falls back to the Substack note. The channel stays selected. |
| `notes[].content` | `string` | Yes | The note body text |
| `notes[].imageUrl` | `string[]` | No | Optional remote image URLs to attach to the note (same as CSV import image_url). WriteStack fetches each URL and stores the image. Max 5. Pass full https:// URLs. Invalid or unreachable URLs are skipped. Max items 5. |
| `notes[].includePreviews` | `boolean` | No | If the note's content contains a link (full https:// URL or bare domain like writestack.io), ask the user whether they want a rich link-preview card (image, title, description) attached before creating/updating the note - do not assume yes. If they confirm, pass includePreviews: true. Prefer writing links as full https:// URLs in the content so previews resolve reliably. Only one preview can be attached per note; if there are multiple links, the first link in the content is used. |
| `notes[].status` | `string` | No | Note status One of: `"draft"`, `"ready"`. Default `"draft"`. |
| `notes[].tags` | `string[]` | No | Category/tag names to assign. Tags also decide which reserved queue times this note can take: a note matches a reserved slot if it shares ANY of the slot's tags. Untagged notes only use open or untagged-only times. Call list_tags first to show available names. |
